thread:
erin: FYI saw another burst of partial streaming responses (206) on /v1/stream/chat this morning 02:17-02:25 UTC. ~520 requests across two AZs. Patterns look familiar to prior incidents.

tom: Can you drop a couple of sample lines and whether this aligns with autoscaler events?

erin: samples: 
```
2026-06-08T02:18:03Z req=ff12 region=us-west-2 status=206 emit_bytes=88 ERR=runtime:emit-interrupted; close=EOF
2026-06-08T02:19:40Z req=ff13 region=us-west-2 status=206 emit_bytes=24 ERR=proxy:forced-drain
```

mike: ops-bot shows a small spike in pod drains at 02:16 UTC in the cluster. Could be the same systemic cause (preempt + immediate drain).

ops-bot: INCIDENT_CREATED: #inc-2026-06-streaming-partial-recurrence (sev3)  responders: @erin @tom @mike

yvonne: Given recurrence, propose a 2-track plan: short-term mitigations (timeout alignment, canary backoff headers, throttle noisy clients) and long-term (stream state telemetry + drain-safe flush). Owners below.

erin: short-term list I added to tracker: 
- edge: return 429+Retry-After for clients opening >40 short streams/min (owner:@tom) 
- gateway: set idle/stream timeouts to 30s canary pool (owner:@mike)
- observability: add "partial_reason" tag and per-stream timeline (owner:@lucas)

tom: I'll implement the edge throttle with a soft 429 and an exponential-backoff header. Can have a canary in 24h. Due 2026-06-11.

mike: Applying timeout alignment to canary cluster now. Will roll 5% traffic and monitor partial_rate. ETA config roll 12h.

lucas: I'll enrich traces with stream states (OPEN, FIRST_CHUNK, LAST_CHUNK, DRAIN_NOTICE, FORCE_CLOSE) and add a dashboard comparing partial_rate vs pod_evictions. Due 2026-06-15.

yvonne: long-term: runtime to implement BestEffortFlush with configurable grace window and emit a final control frame `event:stream_truncated reason=drain` so we can programmatically distinguish forced partials. Owner:@erin due: 2026-06-22.

erin: I'll also add unit/integration tests that simulate mid-stream drain, network jitter, and client reconnect hotspots. Nightly job to run reproducer against staging for 3h.

mike: add a canary stop condition: if partial_rate > 0.3% in canary for 4h, rollback and open debug ticket.

tom: I'll document recommended client behavior in quickstart: backoff with jitter, prefer long-lived single stream over frequent reconnects. Add snippet: 
```
// client backoff pseudocode
sleep = base * 2^attempt + random_jitter()
```

lucas: For detection automation I'll add a weekly job that computes region-level partial_rate and triggers a P0 if > 0.5% delta vs 7-day baseline. This should catch slow regressions.

yvonne: Also adding a postmortem action: runbook update for on-call to include grep examples + join keys for drain logs. Example grep: 
```
rg "status=206" streaming-logs | rg "drain|emit-interrupted|stream_truncated"
```

ops-bot: INCIDENT_UPDATE: ownership assigned and action items added to postmortem tracker.

erin: Scheduling a short sync Tue 10:00 UTC to review canary metrics and initial PRs. If any owner misses due date, escalate to eng leads.

mike: thanks everyone. will post canary link and first 2h snapshot once roll is live.

ops-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: #inc-2026-06-streaming-partial-recurrence (informational)  resolution: mitigations deployed to canary; monitoring enabled; long-term work in trackers.
